Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (14):
get_storybook
Read the book: pages with named layers, activeLayerId and overlay placements, named color profiles (palettes + activePaletteId), asset library (id, name, size), the active page, and webmcp.ready. After a refresh, re-fetch live tools, wait until webmcp.ready is true, then call this to recover asset ids before mutating. Call get_pixel_art_guide first; use get_asset_image and get_page_image to inspect pixels.
get_pixel_art_guide
Load the pixel-art playbook — call this first each session before drawing. Covers composition, palettes, shading, material recipes, character patterns, the draw-look-fix loop, and anti-patterns. Pass topic workflow, shading, composition, or tools; omit for the full playbook.
set_palette
Create or update a named color profile and select it. Pass any number of #rrggbb swatches in colors — there is no count cap, and the built-in Default profile is never overwritten. Pass name (e.g. Bedtime) plus colors to create or update a theme; omit name to update the current non-Default profile, or to create Theme N when Default is active; pass name without colors to select an existing profile including Default. Extra #rrggbb colors can be used inline in draw ops without adding them to the profile first. Optional mood examples: lime #dceeb1, lilac #c5b0f4, cream #f4ecd6, pink #efd4d4, mint #c8e6cd, coral #f3c9b6, navy #1f1d3d, magenta #ff3d8b, plus ink #000000 and paper #ffffff.
add_page
Append a new landscape page and select it. Optional width sets pixel density (48–256; height follows 16:9; default 128); use 160–224 for rich scenes. Compose complex art with add_asset + stamp_assets rather than painting the whole page. Optional story rasterizes one line of words — do not add a story form or caption box on the page.
select_page
Select which page is on the canvas by 0-based index. Use after add_page or when editing a different page. Call get_storybook if you need current indexes.
remove_page
Delete a page by 0-based index. The book must keep at least one page. Returns the updated book summary.
place_text
Rasterize words into the selected layer at x,y (0–1 fractions or pixel coords). Uses Inter glyphs at size 1–8 (default 2). For decorations, draw with rects/lines/fills or stamp assets — do not add a story form or caption box.
get_asset_image
Rasterize an asset to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (optional scale 1–8). Returns JSON stats plus the image, and comma-separated rows as a text fallback. Call after each draw pass (outline → fill → shade → highlight) before stamping.
paint_asset
Paint into an existing asset. Coords are asset-relative (0,0 is top-left). Mix rects (filled blocks), lines (edges), fills (flood), and pixels (fine detail, ≤4096/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. One rect fills any block with no per-pixel cap; color "" erases. Work in passes (outline → fill → shade → highlight); each call returns a PNG — compare before the next pass.
add_asset
Save a reusable sprite to the library (each side 1–96px; library ≤100). Start with template "empty" plus width and height (e.g. 32×32), then paint with paint_asset. Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.

Step 2
Thoughts:
The canvas works by building a scene layer-by-layer rather than drawing a single flat image. Here is the workflow:

### The "Draw, Look, Fix" Loop
1.  **Library of Assets:** Instead of painting on the page, you create reusable "assets" (small sprites). Think of these as building blocks—floor tiles, furniture, plants, and characters.
2.  **Painting Passes:** You don't just "paint." You perform specific passes (outline → fill → shade → highlight) using `paint_asset`. After each call, the system gives you a PNG of the asset so you can inspect your progress before moving to the next pass.
3.  **Stamping Overlays:** Once your assets are ready, you `stamp_assets` onto the page. These are "movable overlays"—they aren't permanently baked into the page pixels, which makes it easy to rearrange your scene or reuse assets (like stamping a plant four times in different spots).
4.  **Scene Composition:** You build your scene back-to-front:
    *   **Layer 1:** Floor tiles (repeat these to fill the ground).
    *   **Layer 2:** Emblems, rugs, and contact shadows.
    *   **Layer 3:** Furniture, counters, and architecture.
    *   **Layer 4:** Characters and plants.

### Essential Tools
*   `add_asset`: Create a blank canvas for a new item.
*   `paint_asset`: Fill that canvas with shapes, lines, and colors.
*   `stamp_assets`: Place your finished items onto your page.
*   `get_page_image`: Use this often. It shows you what the page looks like with all your stamps placed together so you can see if the scene feels full and cohesive.

**The Golden Rule:** Never try to draw a whole scene in one go. Aim for a "dense" scene (12–30+ assets) where items overlap to create depth.

Would you like to start by naming a theme palette for our scene? (e.g., "Cozy Cafe" with some warm browns, creams, and greens?)
Available Tools (14):
get_storybook
Read the book: pages with named layers, activeLayerId and overlay placements, named color profiles (palettes + activePaletteId), asset library (id, name, size), the active page, and webmcp.ready. After a refresh, re-fetch live tools, wait until webmcp.ready is true, then call this to recover asset ids before mutating. Call get_pixel_art_guide first; use get_asset_image and get_page_image to inspect pixels.
get_pixel_art_guide
Load the pixel-art playbook — call this first each session before drawing. Covers composition, palettes, shading, material recipes, character patterns, the draw-look-fix loop, and anti-patterns. Pass topic workflow, shading, composition, or tools; omit for the full playbook.
set_palette
Create or update a named color profile and select it. Pass any number of #rrggbb swatches in colors — there is no count cap, and the built-in Default profile is never overwritten. Pass name (e.g. Bedtime) plus colors to create or update a theme; omit name to update the current non-Default profile, or to create Theme N when Default is active; pass name without colors to select an existing profile including Default. Extra #rrggbb colors can be used inline in draw ops without adding them to the profile first. Optional mood examples: lime #dceeb1, lilac #c5b0f4, cream #f4ecd6, pink #efd4d4, mint #c8e6cd, coral #f3c9b6, navy #1f1d3d, magenta #ff3d8b, plus ink #000000 and paper #ffffff.
add_page
Append a new landscape page and select it. Optional width sets pixel density (48–256; height follows 16:9; default 128); use 160–224 for rich scenes. Compose complex art with add_asset + stamp_assets rather than painting the whole page. Optional story rasterizes one line of words — do not add a story form or caption box on the page.
select_page
Select which page is on the canvas by 0-based index. Use after add_page or when editing a different page. Call get_storybook if you need current indexes.
remove_page
Delete a page by 0-based index. The book must keep at least one page. Returns the updated book summary.
place_text
Rasterize words into the selected layer at x,y (0–1 fractions or pixel coords). Uses Inter glyphs at size 1–8 (default 2). For decorations, draw with rects/lines/fills or stamp assets — do not add a story form or caption box.
get_asset_image
Rasterize an asset to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (optional scale 1–8). Returns JSON stats plus the image, and comma-separated rows as a text fallback. Call after each draw pass (outline → fill → shade → highlight) before stamping.
paint_asset
Paint into an existing asset. Coords are asset-relative (0,0 is top-left). Mix rects (filled blocks), lines (edges), fills (flood), and pixels (fine detail, ≤4096/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. One rect fills any block with no per-pixel cap; color "" erases. Work in passes (outline → fill → shade → highlight); each call returns a PNG — compare before the next pass.
add_asset
Save a reusable sprite to the library (each side 1–96px; library ≤100). Start with template "empty" plus width and height (e.g. 32×32), then paint with paint_asset. Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.

paint_asset
Paint into an existing asset. Coords are asset-relative (0,0 is top-left). Mix rects (filled blocks), lines (edges), fills (flood), and pixels (fine detail, ≤4096/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. One rect fills any block with no per-pixel cap; color "" erases. Work in passes (outline → fill → shade → highlight); each call returns a PNG — compare before the next pass.
add_asset
Save a reusable sprite to the library (each side 1–96px; library ≤100). Start with template "empty" plus width and height (e.g. 32×32), then paint with paint_asset. Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.

Load the pixel-art playbook — call this first each session before drawing. Covers composition, palettes, shading, material recipes, character patterns, the draw-look-fix loop, and anti-patterns. Pass topic workflow, shading, composition, or tools; omit for the full playbook.
set_palette
Create or update a named color profile and select it. Pass any number of #rrggbb swatches in colors — there is no count cap, and the built-in Default profile is never overwritten. Pass name (e.g. Bedtime) plus colors to create or update a theme; omit name to update the current non-Default profile, or to create Theme N when Default is active; pass name without colors to select an existing profile including Default. Extra #rrggbb colors can be used inline in draw ops without adding them to the profile first. Optional mood examples: lime #dceeb1, lilac #c5b0f4, cream #f4ecd6, pink #efd4d4, mint #c8e6cd, coral #f3c9b6, navy #1f1d3d, magenta #ff3d8b, plus ink #000000 and paper #ffffff.
add_page
Append a new landscape page and select it. Optional width sets pixel density (48–256; height follows 16:9; default 128); use 160–224 for rich scenes. Compose complex art with add_asset + stamp_assets rather than painting the whole page. Optional story rasterizes one line of words — do not add a story form or caption box on the page.
select_page
Select which page is on the canvas by 0-based index. Use after add_page or when editing a different page. Call get_storybook if you need current indexes.
remove_page
Delete a page by 0-based index. The book must keep at least one page. Returns the updated book summary.
place_text
Rasterize words into the selected layer at x,y (0–1 fractions or pixel coords). Uses Inter glyphs at size 1–8 (default 2). For decorations, draw with rects/lines/fills or stamp assets — do not add a story form or caption box.
get_asset_image
Rasterize an asset to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (optional scale 1–8). Returns JSON stats plus the image, and comma-separated rows as a text fallback. Call after each draw pass (outline → fill → shade → highlight) before stamping.
paint_asset
Paint into an existing asset. Coords are asset-relative (0,0 is top-left). Mix rects (filled blocks), lines (edges), fills (flood), and pixels (fine detail, ≤4096/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. One rect fills any block with no per-pixel cap; color "" erases. Work in passes (outline → fill → shade → highlight); each call returns a PNG — compare before the next pass.
add_asset
Save a reusable sprite to the library (each side 1–96px; library ≤100). Start with template "empty" plus width and height (e.g. 32×32), then paint with paint_asset. Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.

Available Tools (14):
get_storybook
Read the book: pages with named layers, activeLayerId and overlay placements, named color profiles (palettes + activePaletteId), asset library (id, name, size), the active page, and webmcp.ready. After a refresh, re-fetch live tools, wait until webmcp.ready is true, then call this to recover asset ids before mutating. Call get_pixel_art_guide first; use get_asset_image and get_page_image to inspect pixels.
get_pixel_art_guide
Load the pixel-art playbook — call this first each session before drawing. Covers composition, palettes, shading, material recipes, character patterns, the draw-look-fix loop, and anti-patterns. Pass topic workflow, shading, composition, or tools; omit for the full playbook.
set_palette
Create or update a named color profile and select it. Pass any number of #rrggbb swatches in colors — there is no count cap, and the built-in Default profile is never overwritten. Pass name (e.g. Bedtime) plus colors to create or update a theme; omit name to update the current non-Default profile, or to create Theme N when Default is active; pass name without colors to select an existing profile including Default. Extra #rrggbb colors can be used inline in draw ops without adding them to the profile first. Optional mood examples: lime #dceeb1, lilac #c5b0f4, cream #f4ecd6, pink #efd4d4, mint #c8e6cd, coral #f3c9b6, navy #1f1d3d, magenta #ff3d8b, plus ink #000000 and paper #ffffff.
add_page
Append a new landscape page and select it. Optional width sets pixel density (48–256; height follows 16:9; default 128); use 160–224 for rich scenes. Compose complex art with add_asset + stamp_assets rather than painting the whole page. Optional story rasterizes one line of words — do not add a story form or caption box on the page.
select_page
Select which page is on the canvas by 0-based index. Use after add_page or when editing a different page. Call get_storybook if you need current indexes.
remove_page
Delete a page by 0-based index. The book must keep at least one page. Returns the updated book summary.
place_text
Rasterize words into the selected layer at x,y (0–1 fractions or pixel coords). Uses Inter glyphs at size 1–8 (default 2). For decorations, draw with rects/lines/fills or stamp assets — do not add a story form or caption box.
get_asset_image
Rasterize an asset to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (optional scale 1–8). Returns JSON stats plus the image, and comma-separated rows as a text fallback. Call after each draw pass (outline → fill → shade → highlight) before stamping.
paint_asset
Paint into an existing asset. Coords are asset-relative (0,0 is top-left). Mix rects (filled blocks), lines (edges), fills (flood), and pixels (fine detail, ≤4096/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. One rect fills any block with no per-pixel cap; color "" erases. Work in passes (outline → fill → shade → highlight); each call returns a PNG — compare before the next pass.
add_asset
Save a reusable sprite to the library (each side 1–96px; library ≤100). Start with template "empty" plus width and height (e.g. 32×32), then paint with paint_asset. Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (14):
get_storybook
Read the book: pages with named layers, activeLayerId and overlay placements, named color profiles (palettes + activePaletteId), asset library (id, name, size), the active page, and webmcp.ready. After a refresh, re-fetch live tools, wait until webmcp.ready is true, then call this to recover asset ids before mutating. Call get_pixel_art_guide first; use get_asset_image and get_page_image to inspect pixels.
get_pixel_art_guide
Load the pixel-art playbook — call this first each session before drawing. Covers composition, palettes, shading, material recipes, character patterns, the draw-look-fix loop, and anti-patterns. Pass topic workflow, shading, composition, or tools; omit for the full playbook.
set_palette
Create or update a named color profile and select it. Pass any number of #rrggbb swatches in colors — there is no count cap, and the built-in Default profile is never overwritten. Pass name (e.g. Bedtime) plus colors to create or update a theme; omit name to update the current non-Default profile, or to create Theme N when Default is active; pass name without colors to select an existing profile including Default. Extra #rrggbb colors can be used inline in draw ops without adding them to the profile first. Optional mood examples: lime #dceeb1, lilac #c5b0f4, cream #f4ecd6, pink #efd4d4, mint #c8e6cd, coral #f3c9b6, navy #1f1d3d, magenta #ff3d8b, plus ink #000000 and paper #ffffff.
add_page
Append a new landscape page and select it. Optional width sets pixel density (48–256; height follows 16:9; default 128); use 160–224 for rich scenes. Compose complex art with add_asset + stamp_assets rather than painting the whole page. Optional story rasterizes one line of words — do not add a story form or caption box on the page.
select_page
Select which page is on the canvas by 0-based index. Use after add_page or when editing a different page. Call get_storybook if you need current indexes.
remove_page
Delete a page by 0-based index. The book must keep at least one page. Returns the updated book summary.
place_text
Rasterize words into the selected layer at x,y (0–1 fractions or pixel coords). Uses Inter glyphs at size 1–8 (default 2). For decorations, draw with rects/lines/fills or stamp assets — do not add a story form or caption box.
get_asset_image
Rasterize an asset to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (optional scale 1–8). Returns JSON stats plus the image, and comma-separated rows as a text fallback. Call after each draw pass (outline → fill → shade → highlight) before stamping.
paint_asset
Paint into an existing asset. Coords are asset-relative (0,0 is top-left). Mix rects (filled blocks), lines (edges), fills (flood), and pixels (fine detail, ≤4096/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. One rect fills any block with no per-pixel cap; color "" erases. Work in passes (outline → fill → shade → highlight); each call returns a PNG — compare before the next pass.
add_asset
Save a reusable sprite to the library (each side 1–96px; library ≤100). Start with template "empty" plus width and height (e.g. 32×32), then paint with paint_asset. Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.

Step 2
Available Tools (14):
get_storybook
Read the book: pages with named layers, activeLayerId and overlay placements, named color profiles (palettes + activePaletteId), asset library (id, name, size), the active page, and webmcp.ready. After a refresh, re-fetch live tools, wait until webmcp.ready is true, then call this to recover asset ids before mutating. Call get_pixel_art_guide first; use get_asset_image and get_page_image to inspect pixels.
get_pixel_art_guide
Load the pixel-art playbook — call this first each session before drawing. Covers composition, palettes, shading, material recipes, character patterns, the draw-look-fix loop, and anti-patterns. Pass topic workflow, shading, composition, or tools; omit for the full playbook.
set_palette
Create or update a named color profile and select it. Pass any number of #rrggbb swatches in colors — there is no count cap, and the built-in Default profile is never overwritten. Pass name (e.g. Bedtime) plus colors to create or update a theme; omit name to update the current non-Default profile, or to create Theme N when Default is active; pass name without colors to select an existing profile including Default. Extra #rrggbb colors can be used inline in draw ops without adding them to the profile first. Optional mood examples: lime #dceeb1, lilac #c5b0f4, cream #f4ecd6, pink #efd4d4, mint #c8e6cd, coral #f3c9b6, navy #1f1d3d, magenta #ff3d8b, plus ink #000000 and paper #ffffff.
add_page
Append a new landscape page and select it. Optional width sets pixel density (48–256; height follows 16:9; default 128); use 160–224 for rich scenes. Compose complex art with add_asset + stamp_assets rather than painting the whole page. Optional story rasterizes one line of words — do not add a story form or caption box on the page.
select_page
Select which page is on the canvas by 0-based index. Use after add_page or when editing a different page. Call get_storybook if you need current indexes.
remove_page
Delete a page by 0-based index. The book must keep at least one page. Returns the updated book summary.
place_text
Rasterize words into the selected layer at x,y (0–1 fractions or pixel coords). Uses Inter glyphs at size 1–8 (default 2). For decorations, draw with rects/lines/fills or stamp assets — do not add a story form or caption box.
get_asset_image
Rasterize an asset to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (optional scale 1–8). Returns JSON stats plus the image, and comma-separated rows as a text fallback. Call after each draw pass (outline → fill → shade → highlight) before stamping.
paint_asset
Paint into an existing asset. Coords are asset-relative (0,0 is top-left). Mix rects (filled blocks), lines (edges), fills (flood), and pixels (fine detail, ≤4096/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. One rect fills any block with no per-pixel cap; color "" erases. Work in passes (outline → fill → shade → highlight); each call returns a PNG — compare before the next pass.
add_asset
Save a reusable sprite to the library (each side 1–96px; library ≤100). Start with template "empty" plus width and height (e.g. 32×32), then paint with paint_asset. Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.

Step 4
Available Tools (14):
get_storybook
Read the book: pages with named layers, activeLayerId and overlay placements, named color profiles (palettes + activePaletteId), asset library (id, name, size), the active page, and webmcp.ready. After a refresh, re-fetch live tools, wait until webmcp.ready is true, then call this to recover asset ids before mutating. Call get_pixel_art_guide first; use get_asset_image and get_page_image to inspect pixels.
get_pixel_art_guide
Load the pixel-art playbook — call this first each session before drawing. Covers composition, palettes, shading, material recipes, character patterns, the draw-look-fix loop, and anti-patterns. Pass topic workflow, shading, composition, or tools; omit for the full playbook.
set_palette
Create or update a named color profile and select it. Pass any number of #rrggbb swatches in colors — there is no count cap, and the built-in Default profile is never overwritten. Pass name (e.g. Bedtime) plus colors to create or update a theme; omit name to update the current non-Default profile, or to create Theme N when Default is active; pass name without colors to select an existing profile including Default. Extra #rrggbb colors can be used inline in draw ops without adding them to the profile first. Optional mood examples: lime #dceeb1, lilac #c5b0f4, cream #f4ecd6, pink #efd4d4, mint #c8e6cd, coral #f3c9b6, navy #1f1d3d, magenta #ff3d8b, plus ink #000000 and paper #ffffff.
add_page
Append a new landscape page and select it. Optional width sets pixel density (48–256; height follows 16:9; default 128); use 160–224 for rich scenes. Compose complex art with add_asset + stamp_assets rather than painting the whole page. Optional story rasterizes one line of words — do not add a story form or caption box on the page.
select_page
Select which page is on the canvas by 0-based index. Use after add_page or when editing a different page. Call get_storybook if you need current indexes.
remove_page
Delete a page by 0-based index. The book must keep at least one page. Returns the updated book summary.
place_text
Rasterize words into the selected layer at x,y (0–1 fractions or pixel coords). Uses Inter glyphs at size 1–8 (default 2). For decorations, draw with rects/lines/fills or stamp assets — do not add a story form or caption box.
get_asset_image
Rasterize an asset to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (optional scale 1–8). Returns JSON stats plus the image, and comma-separated rows as a text fallback. Call after each draw pass (outline → fill → shade → highlight) before stamping.
paint_asset
Paint into an existing asset. Coords are asset-relative (0,0 is top-left). Mix rects (filled blocks), lines (edges), fills (flood), and pixels (fine detail, ≤4096/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. One rect fills any block with no per-pixel cap; color "" erases. Work in passes (outline → fill → shade → highlight); each call returns a PNG — compare before the next pass.
add_asset
Save a reusable sprite to the library (each side 1–96px; library ≤100). Start with template "empty" plus width and height (e.g. 32×32), then paint with paint_asset. Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.

Pass name (e.g. Bedtime) plus colors to create or update a theme; omit name to update the current non-Default profile, or to create Theme N when Default is active; pass name without colors to select an existing profile including Default. Extra #rrggbb colors can be used inline in draw ops without adding them to the profile first. Optional mood examples: lime #dceeb1, lilac #c5b0f4, cream #f4ecd6, pink #efd4d4, mint #c8e6cd, coral #f3c9b6, navy #1f1d3d, magenta #ff3d8b, plus ink #000000 and paper #ffffff.
add_page
Append a new landscape page and select it. Optional width sets pixel density (48–256; height follows 16:9; default 128); use 160–224 for rich scenes. Compose complex art with add_asset + stamp_assets rather than painting the whole page. Optional story rasterizes one line of words — do not add a story form or caption box on the page.
select_page
Select which page is on the canvas by 0-based index. Use after add_page or when editing a different page. Call get_storybook if you need current indexes.
remove_page
Delete a page by 0-based index. The book must keep at least one page. Returns the updated book summary.
place_text
Rasterize words into the selected layer at x,y (0–1 fractions or pixel coords). Uses Inter glyphs at size 1–8 (default 2). For decorations, draw with rects/lines/fills or stamp assets — do not add a story form or caption box.
get_asset_image
Rasterize an asset to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (optional scale 1–8). Returns JSON stats plus the image, and comma-separated rows as a text fallback. Call after each draw pass (outline → fill → shade → highlight) before stamping.
paint_asset
Paint into an existing asset. Coords are asset-relative (0,0 is top-left). Mix rects (filled blocks), lines (edges), fills (flood), and pixels (fine detail, ≤4096/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. One rect fills any block with no per-pixel cap; color "" erases. Work in passes (outline → fill → shade → highlight); each call returns a PNG — compare before the next pass.
add_asset
Save a reusable sprite to the library (each side 1–96px; library ≤100). Start with template "empty" plus width and height (e.g. 32×32), then paint with paint_asset. Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (14):
get_storybook
Read the book: pages with named layers, activeLayerId and overlay placements, named color profiles (palettes + activePaletteId), asset library (id, name, size), the active page, and webmcp.ready. After a refresh, re-fetch live tools, wait until webmcp.ready is true, then call this to recover asset ids before mutating. Call get_pixel_art_guide first; use get_asset_image and get_page_image to inspect pixels.
get_pixel_art_guide
Load the pixel-art playbook — call this first each session before drawing. Covers composition, palettes, shading, material recipes, character patterns, the draw-look-fix loop, and anti-patterns. Pass topic workflow, shading, composition, or tools; omit for the full playbook.
set_palette
Create or update a named color profile and select it. Pass any number of #rrggbb swatches in colors — there is no count cap, and the built-in Default profile is never overwritten. Pass name (e.g. Bedtime) plus colors to create or update a theme; omit name to update the current non-Default profile, or to create Theme N when Default is active; pass name without colors to select an existing profile including Default. Extra #rrggbb colors can be used inline in draw ops without adding them to the profile first. Optional mood examples: lime #dceeb1, lilac #c5b0f4, cream #f4ecd6, pink #efd4d4, mint #c8e6cd, coral #f3c9b6, navy #1f1d3d, magenta #ff3d8b, plus ink #000000 and paper #ffffff.
add_page
Append a new landscape page and select it. Optional width sets pixel density (48–256; height follows 16:9; default 128); use 160–224 for rich scenes. Compose complex art with add_asset + stamp_assets rather than painting the whole page. Optional story rasterizes one line of words — do not add a story form or caption box on the page.
select_page
Select which page is on the canvas by 0-based index. Use after add_page or when editing a different page. Call get_storybook if you need current indexes.
remove_page
Delete a page by 0-based index. The book must keep at least one page. Returns the updated book summary.
place_text
Rasterize words into the selected layer at x,y (0–1 fractions or pixel coords). Uses Inter glyphs at size 1–8 (default 2). For decorations, draw with rects/lines/fills or stamp assets — do not add a story form or caption box.
get_asset_image
Rasterize an asset to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (optional scale 1–8). Returns JSON stats plus the image, and comma-separated rows as a text fallback. Call after each draw pass (outline → fill → shade → highlight) before stamping.
paint_asset
Paint into an existing asset. Coords are asset-relative (0,0 is top-left). Mix rects (filled blocks), lines (edges), fills (flood), and pixels (fine detail, ≤4096/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. One rect fills any block with no per-pixel cap; color "" erases. Work in passes (outline → fill → shade → highlight); each call returns a PNG — compare before the next pass.
add_asset
Save a reusable sprite to the library (each side 1–96px; library ≤100). Start with template "empty" plus width and height (e.g. 32×32), then paint with paint_asset. Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.

Rasterize an asset to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (optional scale 1–8). Returns JSON stats plus the image, and comma-separated rows as a text fallback. Call after each draw pass (outline → fill → shade → highlight) before stamping.
paint_asset
Paint into an existing asset. Coords are asset-relative (0,0 is top-left). Mix rects (filled blocks), lines (edges), fills (flood), and pixels (fine detail, ≤4096/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. One rect fills any block with no per-pixel cap; color "" erases. Work in passes (outline → fill → shade → highlight); each call returns a PNG — compare before the next pass.
add_asset
Save a reusable sprite to the library (each side 1–96px; library ≤100). Start with template "empty" plus width and height (e.g. 32×32), then paint with paint_asset. Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.

get_storybook

Call get_pixel_art_guide first; use get_asset_image and get_page_image to inspect pixels.
get_pixel_art_guide
Load the pixel-art playbook — call this first each session before drawing. Covers composition, palettes, shading, material recipes, character patterns, the draw-look-fix loop, and anti-patterns. Pass topic workflow, shading, composition, or tools; omit for the full playbook.
set_palette
Create or update a named color profile and select it. Pass any number of #rrggbb swatches in colors — there is no count cap, and the built-in Default profile is never overwritten. Pass name (e.g. Bedtime) plus colors to create or update a theme; omit name to update the current non-Default profile, or to create Theme N when Default is active; pass name without colors to select an existing profile including Default. Extra #rrggbb colors can be used inline in draw ops without adding them to the profile first. Optional mood examples: lime #dceeb1, lilac #c5b0f4, cream #f4ecd6, pink #efd4d4, mint #c8e6cd, coral #f3c9b6, navy #1f1d3d, magenta #ff3d8b, plus ink #000000 and paper #ffffff.
add_page
Append a new landscape page and select it. Optional width sets pixel density (48–256; height follows 16:9; default 128); use 160–224 for rich scenes. Compose complex art with add_asset + stamp_assets rather than painting the whole page. Optional story rasterizes one line of words — do not add a story form or caption box on the page.
select_page
Select which page is on the canvas by 0-based index. Use after add_page or when editing a different page. Call get_storybook if you need current indexes.
remove_page
Delete a page by 0-based index. The book must keep at least one page. Returns the updated book summary.

Append a new landscape page and select it. Optional width sets pixel density (48–256; height follows 16:9; default 128); use 160–224 for rich scenes. Compose complex art with add_asset + stamp_assets rather than painting the whole page. Optional story rasterizes one line of words — do not add a story form or caption box on the page.
select_page
Select which page is on the canvas by 0-based index. Use after add_page or when editing a different page. Call get_storybook if you need current indexes.
remove_page
Delete a page by 0-based index. The book must keep at least one page. Returns the updated book summary.
place_text
Rasterize words into the selected layer at x,y (0–1 fractions or pixel coords). Uses Inter glyphs at size 1–8 (default 2). For decorations, draw with rects/lines/fills or stamp assets — do not add a story form or caption box.
get_asset_image
Rasterize an asset to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (optional scale 1–8). Returns JSON stats plus the image, and comma-separated rows as a text fallback. Call after each draw pass (outline → fill → shade → highlight) before stamping.
paint_asset
Paint into an existing asset. Coords are asset-relative (0,0 is top-left). Mix rects (filled blocks), lines (edges), fills (flood), and pixels (fine detail, ≤4096/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. One rect fills any block with no per-pixel cap; color "" erases. Work in passes (outline → fill → shade → highlight); each call returns a PNG — compare before the next pass.
add_asset
Save a reusable sprite to the library (each side 1–96px; library ≤100). Start with template "empty" plus width and height (e.g. 32×32), then paint with paint_asset. Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (14):
get_storybook
Read the book: pages with named layers, activeLayerId and overlay placements, named color profiles (palettes + activePaletteId), asset library (id, name, size), the active page, and webmcp.ready. After a refresh, re-fetch live tools, wait until webmcp.ready is true, then call this to recover asset ids before mutating. Call get_pixel_art_guide first; use get_asset_image and get_page_image to inspect pixels.
get_pixel_art_guide
Load the pixel-art playbook — call this first each session before drawing. Covers composition, palettes, shading, material recipes, character patterns, the draw-look-fix loop, and anti-patterns. Pass topic workflow, shading, composition, or tools; omit for the full playbook.
set_palette
Create or update a named color profile and select it. Pass any number of #rrggbb swatches in colors — there is no count cap, and the built-in Default profile is never overwritten. Pass name (e.g. Bedtime) plus colors to create or update a theme; omit name to update the current non-Default profile, or to create Theme N when Default is active; pass name without colors to select an existing profile including Default. Extra #rrggbb colors can be used inline in draw ops without adding them to the profile first. Optional mood examples: lime #dceeb1, lilac #c5b0f4, cream #f4ecd6, pink #efd4d4, mint #c8e6cd, coral #f3c9b6, navy #1f1d3d, magenta #ff3d8b, plus ink #000000 and paper #ffffff.
add_page
Append a new landscape page and select it. Optional width sets pixel density (48–256; height follows 16:9; default 128); use 160–224 for rich scenes. Compose complex art with add_asset + stamp_assets rather than painting the whole page. Optional story rasterizes one line of words — do not add a story form or caption box on the page.
select_page
Select which page is on the canvas by 0-based index. Use after add_page or when editing a different page. Call get_storybook if you need current indexes.
remove_page
Delete a page by 0-based index. The book must keep at least one page. Returns the updated book summary.
place_text
Rasterize words into the selected layer at x,y (0–1 fractions or pixel coords). Uses Inter glyphs at size 1–8 (default 2). For decorations, draw with rects/lines/fills or stamp assets — do not add a story form or caption box.
get_asset_image
Rasterize an asset to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (optional scale 1–8). Returns JSON stats plus the image, and comma-separated rows as a text fallback. Call after each draw pass (outline → fill → shade → highlight) before stamping.
paint_asset
Paint into an existing asset. Coords are asset-relative (0,0 is top-left). Mix rects (filled blocks), lines (edges), fills (flood), and pixels (fine detail, ≤4096/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. One rect fills any block with no per-pixel cap; color "" erases. Work in passes (outline → fill → shade → highlight); each call returns a PNG — compare before the next pass.
add_asset
Save a reusable sprite to the library (each side 1–96px; library ≤100). Start with template "empty" plus width and height (e.g. 32×32), then paint with paint_asset. Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.

Step 3
Available Tools (14):
get_storybook
Read the book: pages with named layers, activeLayerId and overlay placements, named color profiles (palettes + activePaletteId), asset library (id, name, size), the active page, and webmcp.ready. After a refresh, re-fetch live tools, wait until webmcp.ready is true, then call this to recover asset ids before mutating. Call get_pixel_art_guide first; use get_asset_image and get_page_image to inspect pixels.
get_pixel_art_guide
Load the pixel-art playbook — call this first each session before drawing. Covers composition, palettes, shading, material recipes, character patterns, the draw-look-fix loop, and anti-patterns. Pass topic workflow, shading, composition, or tools; omit for the full playbook.
set_palette
Create or update a named color profile and select it. Pass any number of #rrggbb swatches in colors — there is no count cap, and the built-in Default profile is never overwritten. Pass name (e.g. Bedtime) plus colors to create or update a theme; omit name to update the current non-Default profile, or to create Theme N when Default is active; pass name without colors to select an existing profile including Default. Extra #rrggbb colors can be used inline in draw ops without adding them to the profile first. Optional mood examples: lime #dceeb1, lilac #c5b0f4, cream #f4ecd6, pink #efd4d4, mint #c8e6cd, coral #f3c9b6, navy #1f1d3d, magenta #ff3d8b, plus ink #000000 and paper #ffffff.
add_page
Append a new landscape page and select it. Optional width sets pixel density (48–256; height follows 16:9; default 128); use 160–224 for rich scenes. Compose complex art with add_asset + stamp_assets rather than painting the whole page. Optional story rasterizes one line of words — do not add a story form or caption box on the page.
select_page
Select which page is on the canvas by 0-based index. Use after add_page or when editing a different page. Call get_storybook if you need current indexes.
remove_page
Delete a page by 0-based index. The book must keep at least one page. Returns the updated book summary.
place_text
Rasterize words into the selected layer at x,y (0–1 fractions or pixel coords). Uses Inter glyphs at size 1–8 (default 2). For decorations, draw with rects/lines/fills or stamp assets — do not add a story form or caption box.
get_asset_image
Rasterize an asset to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (optional scale 1–8). Returns JSON stats plus the image, and comma-separated rows as a text fallback. Call after each draw pass (outline → fill → shade → highlight) before stamping.
paint_asset
Paint into an existing asset. Coords are asset-relative (0,0 is top-left). Mix rects (filled blocks), lines (edges), fills (flood), and pixels (fine detail, ≤4096/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. One rect fills any block with no per-pixel cap; color "" erases. Work in passes (outline → fill → shade → highlight); each call returns a PNG — compare before the next pass.
add_asset
Save a reusable sprite to the library (each side 1–96px; library ≤100). Start with template "empty" plus width and height (e.g. 32×32), then paint with paint_asset. Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.

Available Tools (14):
get_storybook
Read the book: pages with named layers, activeLayerId and overlay placements, named color profiles (palettes + activePaletteId), asset library (id, name, size), the active page, and webmcp.ready. After a refresh, re-fetch live tools, wait until webmcp.ready is true, then call this to recover asset ids before mutating. Call get_pixel_art_guide first; use get_asset_image and get_page_image to inspect pixels.
get_pixel_art_guide
Load the pixel-art playbook — call this first each session before drawing. Covers composition, palettes, shading, material recipes, character patterns, the draw-look-fix loop, and anti-patterns. Pass topic workflow, shading, composition, or tools; omit for the full playbook.
set_palette
Create or update a named color profile and select it. Pass any number of #rrggbb swatches in colors — there is no count cap, and the built-in Default profile is never overwritten. Pass name (e.g. Bedtime) plus colors to create or update a theme; omit name to update the current non-Default profile, or to create Theme N when Default is active; pass name without colors to select an existing profile including Default. Extra #rrggbb colors can be used inline in draw ops without adding them to the profile first. Optional mood examples: lime #dceeb1, lilac #c5b0f4, cream #f4ecd6, pink #efd4d4, mint #c8e6cd, coral #f3c9b6, navy #1f1d3d, magenta #ff3d8b, plus ink #000000 and paper #ffffff.
add_page
Append a new landscape page and select it. Optional width sets pixel density (48–256; height follows 16:9; default 128); use 160–224 for rich scenes. Compose complex art with add_asset + stamp_assets rather than painting the whole page. Optional story rasterizes one line of words — do not add a story form or caption box on the page.
select_page
Select which page is on the canvas by 0-based index. Use after add_page or when editing a different page. Call get_storybook if you need current indexes.
remove_page
Delete a page by 0-based index. The book must keep at least one page. Returns the updated book summary.
place_text
Rasterize words into the selected layer at x,y (0–1 fractions or pixel coords). Uses Inter glyphs at size 1–8 (default 2). For decorations, draw with rects/lines/fills or stamp assets — do not add a story form or caption box.
get_asset_image
Rasterize an asset to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (optional scale 1–8). Returns JSON stats plus the image, and comma-separated rows as a text fallback. Call after each draw pass (outline → fill → shade → highlight) before stamping.
paint_asset
Paint into an existing asset. Coords are asset-relative (0,0 is top-left). Mix rects (filled blocks), lines (edges), fills (flood), and pixels (fine detail, ≤4096/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. One rect fills any block with no per-pixel cap; color "" erases. Work in passes (outline → fill → shade → highlight); each call returns a PNG — compare before the next pass.
add_asset
Save a reusable sprite to the library (each side 1–96px; library ≤100). Start with template "empty" plus width and height (e.g. 32×32), then paint with paint_asset. Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.

Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.

Step 2
Available Tools (14):
get_storybook
Read the book: pages with named layers, activeLayerId and overlay placements, named color profiles (palettes + activePaletteId), asset library (id, name, size), the active page, and webmcp.ready. After a refresh, re-fetch live tools, wait until webmcp.ready is true, then call this to recover asset ids before mutating. Call get_pixel_art_guide first; use get_asset_image and get_page_image to inspect pixels.
get_pixel_art_guide
Load the pixel-art playbook — call this first each session before drawing. Covers composition, palettes, shading, material recipes, character patterns, the draw-look-fix loop, and anti-patterns. Pass topic workflow, shading, composition, or tools; omit for the full playbook.
set_palette
Create or update a named color profile and select it. Pass any number of #rrggbb swatches in colors — there is no count cap, and the built-in Default profile is never overwritten. Pass name (e.g. Bedtime) plus colors to create or update a theme; omit name to update the current non-Default profile, or to create Theme N when Default is active; pass name without colors to select an existing profile including Default. Extra #rrggbb colors can be used inline in draw ops without adding them to the profile first. Optional mood examples: lime #dceeb1, lilac #c5b0f4, cream #f4ecd6, pink #efd4d4, mint #c8e6cd, coral #f3c9b6, navy #1f1d3d, magenta #ff3d8b, plus ink #000000 and paper #ffffff.
add_page
Append a new landscape page and select it. Optional width sets pixel density (48–256; height follows 16:9; default 128); use 160–224 for rich scenes. Compose complex art with add_asset + stamp_assets rather than painting the whole page. Optional story rasterizes one line of words — do not add a story form or caption box on the page.
select_page
Select which page is on the canvas by 0-based index. Use after add_page or when editing a different page. Call get_storybook if you need current indexes.
remove_page
Delete a page by 0-based index. The book must keep at least one page. Returns the updated book summary.
place_text
Rasterize words into the selected layer at x,y (0–1 fractions or pixel coords). Uses Inter glyphs at size 1–8 (default 2). For decorations, draw with rects/lines/fills or stamp assets — do not add a story form or caption box.
get_asset_image
Rasterize an asset to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (optional scale 1–8). Returns JSON stats plus the image, and comma-separated rows as a text fallback. Call after each draw pass (outline → fill → shade → highlight) before stamping.
paint_asset
Paint into an existing asset. Coords are asset-relative (0,0 is top-left). Mix rects (filled blocks), lines (edges), fills (flood), and pixels (fine detail, ≤4096/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. One rect fills any block with no per-pixel cap; color "" erases. Work in passes (outline → fill → shade → highlight); each call returns a PNG — compare before the next pass.
add_asset
Save a reusable sprite to the library (each side 1–96px; library ≤100). Start with template "empty" plus width and height (e.g. 32×32), then paint with paint_asset. Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.

Available Tools (14):
get_storybook
Read the book: pages with named layers, activeLayerId and overlay placements, named color profiles (palettes + activePaletteId), asset library (id, name, size), the active page, and webmcp.ready. After a refresh, re-fetch live tools, wait until webmcp.ready is true, then call this to recover asset ids before mutating. Call get_pixel_art_guide first; use get_asset_image and get_page_image to inspect pixels.
get_pixel_art_guide
Load the pixel-art playbook — call this first each session before drawing. Covers composition, palettes, shading, material recipes, character patterns, the draw-look-fix loop, and anti-patterns. Pass topic workflow, shading, composition, or tools; omit for the full playbook.
set_palette
Create or update a named color profile and select it. Pass any number of #rrggbb swatches in colors — there is no count cap, and the built-in Default profile is never overwritten. Pass name (e.g. Bedtime) plus colors to create or update a theme; omit name to update the current non-Default profile, or to create Theme N when Default is active; pass name without colors to select an existing profile including Default. Extra #rrggbb colors can be used inline in draw ops without adding them to the profile first. Optional mood examples: lime #dceeb1, lilac #c5b0f4, cream #f4ecd6, pink #efd4d4, mint #c8e6cd, coral #f3c9b6, navy #1f1d3d, magenta #ff3d8b, plus ink #000000 and paper #ffffff.
add_page
Append a new landscape page and select it. Optional width sets pixel density (48–256; height follows 16:9; default 128); use 160–224 for rich scenes. Compose complex art with add_asset + stamp_assets rather than painting the whole page. Optional story rasterizes one line of words — do not add a story form or caption box on the page.
select_page
Select which page is on the canvas by 0-based index. Use after add_page or when editing a different page. Call get_storybook if you need current indexes.
remove_page
Delete a page by 0-based index. The book must keep at least one page. Returns the updated book summary.
place_text
Rasterize words into the selected layer at x,y (0–1 fractions or pixel coords). Uses Inter glyphs at size 1–8 (default 2). For decorations, draw with rects/lines/fills or stamp assets — do not add a story form or caption box.
get_asset_image
Rasterize an asset to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (optional scale 1–8). Returns JSON stats plus the image, and comma-separated rows as a text fallback. Call after each draw pass (outline → fill → shade → highlight) before stamping.
paint_asset
Paint into an existing asset. Coords are asset-relative (0,0 is top-left). Mix rects (filled blocks), lines (edges), fills (flood), and pixels (fine detail, ≤4096/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. One rect fills any block with no per-pixel cap; color "" erases. Work in passes (outline → fill → shade → highlight); each call returns a PNG — compare before the next pass.
add_asset
Save a reusable sprite to the library (each side 1–96px; library ≤100). Start with template "empty" plus width and height (e.g. 32×32), then paint with paint_asset. Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.

Also accepts comma-separated rows, a flat pixels array, a solid fill, or a copy of a page rect (x, y, width, height). Painted assets return an inline PNG — compare before the next pass.
stamp_assets
Add movable overlay placements on the selected layer of the active page (max 100 per call) — they are NOT baked into page.pixels. Each item needs id, x, y; optional scale (default 1 = native size) or width/height. Array order is z-index, back-to-front: floor tiles → emblem/shadows → furniture → plants/characters. Transparent asset pixels do not punch holes. Repeat the same asset (plants ×4). On failure, reports which stamp index failed.
remove_asset
Remove a sprite from the library by id. Overlay placements that referenced it are dropped; pixels already baked into page.pixels stay. Call get_storybook for valid ids.
paint_page
Paint into the selected layer of the active page for flat backgrounds and touch-ups. Mix rects, lines, fills, and pixels (≤4096 detail pixels/call); ops apply rects → lines → fills → pixels. color "" erases; a full-page rect with "" clears the selected layer. For characters and props, build assets then stamp_assets. Optional offsetX/offsetY tiles a motif across the page.
get_page_image
Rasterize a page to PNG so you can compare it to a reference (composites overlay stamps over page.pixels). Omit x, y, width, height for the full page; pass all four to crop a region. Returns coverage, colorCount, placementCount, and sceneHint (few placements, huge stamps, full-page painting, or noisy colorCount). Call after every few stamps, not only at the end.
